title: autotune: default batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, initial quantization profile templates, and a unit-economics analysis CLI used by ops and SRE to validate cost impact. Backwards compatible; runtime falls back to existing configs if autotune is disabled.
description:
Motivation: Make cost-optimization recommendations first-class by shipping safe defaults for batching and KV caching and providing reproducible quantization profiles and unit-economics tooling. This PR implements a conservative autotune path that updates runtime defaults (batch size heuristics, cache retention) and ships a small CLI (tools/uecon) to estimate per-token cost and ROI for model+quant+batch settings.

Summary of changes: 1) Add autotune defaults module and config layer integrations so Dedicated/Hosted can apply safe defaults without customer changes. 2) Introduce quantization profile templates and lookup by model family (ops/quant/profiles.toml). 3) Implement unit-economics CLI (tools/uecon/cli.py) to compute per-request token cost, expected throughput, and savings projections. 4) Wire runtime heuristics to prefer batching/caching settings that respect latency SLOs via load-aware rules. 5) Add E2E tests and benchmark harnesses for the new defaults.

Commits: ["feat(autotune): add defaults module and API", "feat(quant): add base quant profiles and templating", "feat(uecon): unit-econ CLI and reporting", "test: add unit + integration tests for autotune", "ci: update pipeline to run uecon smoke tests"]

Files changed (high level): ["runtime/autotune/defaults.py", "runtime/batching/batcher.cpp", "runtime/caching/kv_cache_manager.py", "ops/quant/profiles.toml", "tools/uecon/cli.py", "docs/optimizations/autotune.md", "tests/autotune/test_defaults.py", "benchmarks/autotune/latency_vs_cost.ipynb"]

Small snippets: runtime/autotune/defaults.py exposes a small public function get_autotune_config(request_context) which returns a namespaced config used by the serving path. Example usage in routing layer: 

  cfg = get_autotune_config(req.context)
  batcher.configure(cfg.batch)
  kv_cache.set_policy(cfg.cache)

(Implementation keeps existing explicit config precedence: user config > tenant defaults > autotune defaults > global fallback.)

Testing & benchmarks: Ran the perf-canary harness on an rtx-8000-like setup (8xA100 equivalent). With autotune enabled and conservative defaults we observed median token cost reduction of ~21% for a conversational workload with 1.6x batching improvement and <5% p95 latency regression due to adaptive batching windows. Benchmarks and notebooks in benchmarks/autotune show the methodology and raw numbers.

Review conversation highlights: 
- Ethan Li (reviewer): asked for clarity on precedence and a stronger opt-out path for enterprise customers behind a feature flag.
- Author (Priya): clarified precedence in comments and added a feature-flag gate and integration test to ensure explicit tenant configs are honored.
- Marisol: requested additional metrics (per-route effective batch size and cache-hit rate) surfaced in console to validate autotune in production.
- Priya: added two new metrics points and updated docs/optimizations/autotune.md with dashboards and example queries.
- Samir: did a safety pass on quant profiles and suggested pinning aggressive profiles behind config until we collect more evals. Priya updated profiles.toml to include conservative and experimental buckets and documented rollout guidance.

Code review outcome: approvals from Ethan and Marisol after follow-ups. CI initially failed on the new uecon smoke test (flaky network dependency); fixed by stubbing external pricing endpoint and re-running. Final CI status: all checks passed.

CI checks summary: ["build: pass", "unit tests: pass (coverage 86%)", "integration tests: pass", "benchmarks: smoke pass", "lint: pass"]

Merge: squash-merged to main. Merge commit updates changelog and adds docs reference. Merge method: squash.

Related: Linear ENG-1245 tracks the autotune roadmap; ENG-1299 tracks unit-econ integrations with billing/analytics teams. No linked JIRA for customer support on this change.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: Autotune defaults are disabled by default for new Dedicated clusters; Hosted rollout on a small percentage of traffic behind a config flag controlled by ops. The uecon CLI is opt-in and intended for SRE/solutions to validate cost tradeoffs before enabling. The PR includes a small migration note in docs/optimizations/autotune.md explaining safe rollout steps.

notes_for_ops: Autotune defaults are behind a config flag (autotune.enabled). Hosted rollout will be phased (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with extra logging. If customers report latency regressions, disable autotune per-tenant via tenant config or set autotune.mode=off.
benchmarks_summary: Conservative defaults produced ~21% token cost reduction for conversational workloads in our lab with <5% p95 latency tail impact; full benchmark notebook included in benchmarks/autotune.
human_readable_changes: High level: safer defaults for batching/caching, quant profile templates, UEcon CLI for per-token cost estimates, metrics and docs for rollout.
qa_notes: Added unit + integration tests. Recommended QA: run benchmarks against a small dedicated pool with representative traffic, validate console metrics, and run uecon CLI with customer pricing file.
